official.deadline_note: The ARUA page publishes no calendar deadline: it states the application round 'usually opens in early February each year' and that applicants 'will not be able to apply until you have received the email with the link to the scholarship application portal in February'. The application link is published on the Lund University Global Scholarship page once the round opens. The related study-application deadline at universityadmissions.se is 15 January, with the application fee and supporting documents due in early February. Per the Global Scholarship page (which hosts the portal link and runs the shared February round), the most recent round closed on 16 February 2026; the next round is expected in early February 2027 but no exact date has been published.
official.application_cycle: Annual February round for the following autumn intake: study application by 15 January, fee and documents early February, scholarship round early February. The 2026 scholarship round closed 16 February 2026; the next round is expected early February 2027 for autumn 2027 entry.
official.status_note: As of 10 October 2026 the scholarship application round is closed. The Lund University Global Scholarship page, which is where the application-portal link for the ARUA round is published, states 'The Lund University scholarship application is now closed. The deadline to apply was 16 February 2026.' The ARUA page (last updated 6 October 2026) still states that the round 'usually opens in early February each year', so the next round is expected in February 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Lund's exact wording: 'The ARUA Scholarship covers a percentage of the tuition fees, up to a maximum of 90%. The exact percentage awarded depends on the available budget of the programme/faculty concerned.' The Global Scholarship page states 'Scholarships cover tuition fees only - living costs are not included' and that 'the scholarship amount will be deducted from your Lund University tuition fee invoice automatically'.
benefits: The ARUA Scholarship covers a percentage of the tuition fees, up to a maximum of 90%.

eligibility: Be or have been a student at an ARUA university in one of the countries listed on the Lund ARUA page (Ethiopia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda).
Be a citizen of a country from outside the EU/EEA (and Switzerland) and be required to pay tuition fees for your studies at Lund University.
Have submitted a correct, complete and timely application for an international degree programme at Lund University.
Have selected Lund University as your first choice in your application at universityadmissions.se.
Lund states: 'Please do not apply if you do not meet all of the above requirements. Your application will not be considered.'
requirements: A correct, complete and timely application for an international degree programme at Lund University, with Lund University selected as first choice on universityadmissions.se.

A personal 'scholarship motivation video' of maximum 1 minute uploaded to an open source video sharing platform such as YouTube or Vimeo, with the video link included in the scholarship application form.
The motivation video should explain why your academic achievements and reasons for applying to Lund University make you a suitable potential recipient.
As the scholarship is merit-based only, your financial situation/challenges must not be presented in the video.
Non-EU citizens must pay the application fee, or submit proof of exemption, by the early-February deadline for autumn studies.
documents: Application fee payment, or proof of exemption, submitted by the early-February deadline - Lund states the application will not be processed until this is done.
Official transcripts and certificates, submitted to University Admissions in Sweden according to the country-specific instructions (not sent directly to Lund University).

Proof of English proficiency, e.g. IELTS Academic total score 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL iBT 20 in the written test with a total score of 90, arriving by the supporting-document deadline.
Additional documents for final-year Bachelor's students applying to a Master's programme.
Programme-specific supporting documents where the programme requires them, e.g. statement of purpose, CV, letters of recommendation or a writing sample.
A portfolio of work for a few programmes, mainly in architecture and design, usually sent directly to the programme administrator at Lund University.
The link to the one-minute scholarship motivation video hosted on an open source video platform.
selection_criteria: Priority is given to students with strong academic performance.
Applicants judged to be a good fit for the programme they have applied for.
Applicants who show a strong commitment and desire to study at Lund University.
Applicants who have selected a programme at Lund University as their first choice at universityadmissions.se.
The scholarship is merit-based only - financial need is not considered in the selection process.
coverage: Tuition fees: a percentage of the tuition fees, up to a maximum of 90%.
The exact percentage awarded depends on the available budget of the programme/faculty concerned.
Living costs are explicitly not covered - recipients must still have the means to cover their living costs according to the requirements of the Swedish Migration Agency.
The scholarship amount is deducted from the Lund University tuition fee invoice automatically; no travel, insurance or installation allowance is published.
application_method: Apply for an international degree programme at Lund University through universityadmissions.se, ranking Lund University as your first choice; the application deadline for studies is 15 January.
Pay the application fee and submit supporting documents by the early-February deadline.

Wait for the email with the link to the Lund University scholarship application portal, which opens in early February; the link is also published on the Lund University Global Scholarship page once the round opens.
Submit the scholarship application in the Lund scholarship application portal (a separate portal from universityadmissions.se), including the link to your maximum 1-minute motivation video.
official.application_route: Apply first to an international degree programme at universityadmissions.se with Lund as first choice (deadline 15 January), then apply through the separate Lund University scholarship application portal when the February round opens, submitting a maximum 1-minute motivation video link.
official.citizenship_residency: You must be a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA (and Switzerland) and therefore be required to pay tuition fees at Lund University, and you must be or have been a student at an ARUA member university in one of the 13 listed African countries.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is aimed at international students: it requires citizenship of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, tuition-fee liability at Lund University, and current or previous enrolment at an ARUA member university in one of the listed African countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction is published. The restriction is institutional: you must be or have been a student at an ARUA member university in one of the listed countries. Lund notes that its list 'may not reflect the latest changes' and directs applicants to the ARUA website for the most up-to-date list of member universities.
official.duration: The page does not publish a fixed award duration; the waiver applies to the tuition fees of the Lund University programme the applicant is admitted to.
official.description: Lund University offers a scholarship programme for high-achieving African students from renowned research-oriented universities in a number of African countries, aimed at providing financial support to prospective students who have demonstrated academic excellence at one of the member universities of the African Research Universities Alliance (ARUA). The scholarship is selective and merit-based and is intended for African students who are committed to Lund University, and it covers a percentage of tuition fees up to a maximum of 90% but not living costs.
official.region: Sweden (host); applicants from the 13 listed African countries
official.program_type: University tuition-fee scholarship (partial, merit-based) within the Lund University Global Scholarship framework, restricted to students of listed ARUA member universities
official.english_requirement: The ARUA page sets no separate scholarship English test. Lund University requires degree-programme English proficiency equivalent to at least English 6/English level 2: IELTS (Academic) total score 6.5 with no section less than 5.5, TOEFL internet-based 20 in the written test with a total score of 90, or previous upper secondary or university studies; some programmes require a higher level, for example English Level 7. The deadline for proof of English is the same as the deadline for receipt of supporting documentation.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition discount, not a stipend: the real prize is having up to 90% of your Lund tuition fee wiped off the invoice, while you independently prove to the Swedish Migration Agency that you can fund your own living costs. Your two earliest decisions decide whether you can even apply - studying at one of the 13 listed ARUA universities, and ranking Lund first on universityadmissions.se by 15 January. Everything after that hinges on a 60-second video that argues academic merit, because Lund explicitly ignores financial hardship when it scores candidates, so a needs-based pitch wastes the only material you submit.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates of the 13 listed ARUA member universities with strong transcripts who are willing to rank Lund first and can condense their academic case into a tight one-minute video.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your ARUA university and country still appear on Lund's list, and cross-check the current membership on arua.org/member-universities before you rely on eligibility.

Rank Lund University first on universityadmissions.se and pay the application fee, or file fee-exemption proof, by the early-February deadline - an unpaid fee means your application is not processed at all.
Script and rehearse a 60-second video that argues academic achievement and commitment to Lund; cut every reference to financial need.
Upload the finished video to a public platform such as YouTube or Vimeo and paste the exact link into the scholarship form.
Book an English test early enough that IELTS/TOEFL results reach University Admissions in Sweden by the supporting-document deadline, since that deadline is the same one.
Build a documented living-cost funding plan you could show the Migration Agency, because the award covers tuition only.
common_rejection_risks: Ranking another university first on universityadmissions.se - Lund treats first-choice status as a hard prerequisite, not a preference.
Missing the fee or exemption deadline in early February, since Lund will not process the application until it is settled.
Losing the short February scholarship window because the round is reachable only through the emailed portal link or the link posted on the Global Scholarship page.
Spending the 60-second video on financial hardship, which the university states is not considered in selection.
Applying from an ARUA university or country that has dropped off Lund's list.
Late documents when your country requires hard-copy transcripts to University Admissions in Sweden rather than an upload.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: All living costs (housing, food, insurance and personal expenses), plus whatever share of tuition remains below the 90% maximum, the application fee if you are not exempt, flights and residence-permit costs. Lund publishes a living-costs page for budgeting and points recipients to the Swedish Migration Agency's financial requirement, which must be met independently of this award.
document_audit: Transcripts and certificates go to University Admissions in Sweden, not to Lund - sending them to Lund directly does not count.
Several countries must send hard copies or have their own university email documents directly, so a scanned upload may not be accepted; read the country instructions first.
A letter from your university saying you studied in English is often not accepted as proof of English proficiency, so plan for an actual test.
Architecture and design programmes require a portfolio sent straight to the programme administrator, bypassing the national portal.
Final-year Bachelor's applicants need the extra proof of ongoing studies by the same document deadline.
You may hold only one ARUA scholarship per application round, so choose the programme you are betting on rather than spreading applications.
alerts: The awarded percentage is driven by programme or faculty budget, so two equally strong applicants in different faculties can receive very different waivers.
Results arrive in the same email as the Lund University Global Scholarship, so do not sit waiting for a separate ARUA message.
For scholarship holders the remaining tuition instalment can fall due earlier than the standard non-scholarship payment date.
You must accept the scholarship within the timeframe in the award letter and accept the study place, or the offer lapses.
There is no standalone ARUA application URL - the round opens only through the February email and the link published on the Global Scholarship page.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: universityadmissions.se by 15 January with Lund first, fee and documents in early February, emailed Lund scholarship portal link in February, one-minute video link submitted, then a single combined LUGS/ARUA decision email shortly after admission results.
